This Shelby GT350 Just Sold for Hilariously Cheap – But There’s a Catch
13 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Are you still dreaming about buying that nice Shelby GT3 50 version of the S550 Ford Mustang? Well, this could be a great time to do that, as the value of this model has dipped. And it has done so significantly to the point where it is cheaper than a Toyota Corolla.
We kid you not, this example just sold for nothing at an online auction in the United States of America. The window sticker reveals that it initially went for $60,740, yet when the gavel hit the table on October 20, 2026, it changed hands for a mere $27,753. That’s less than half compared to what it initially cost. But why did it go for that low when these things usually sell for $55,000 to $60,000 in today’s used car market in the USA?
Well, first and foremost, it is not exactly a low mileage car. This Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 had 113,700 miles (183,000 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging, so it has seen a lot of action over the years. The seller bought it in November 2020, adding some 85,600 miles (137,800 km) since, and he said that he “never had a single issue with this car in the six years of ownership,” adding that “it has been stored outside for the past few years, but covered and in shade most of the time.”
Second, it is not exactly in top-notch condition either, but you probably know that, given the high mileage. The muscle car in question is said to have been listed as a manufacturer buyback vehicle in September 2020, with the seller noting that the reason was “excessive tapping sound heard from the engine.” This ride currently carries a Manufacturer Buyback title from the Florida DMV. It also has chips and scratches on the outside, a dent on the left rear three-quarter panel, and wear on the driver’s seat and interior touch points.
Photo: Cars&Bids And third, it also has quite a few mods, and most of the time, these do not tend to attract real petrolheads. Quite the opposite, in fact. The cat-delete mid pipes, a new exhaust system, a cold air intake system, an aftermarket coolant tank, clear taillights, and the rear spoiler are said to have come from the aftermarket world on this Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 , which is a 2017 model year car, by the way. The seller also notes that the windows have been tinted.
The muscle car features an Avalanche Gray paint finish on the outside, complemented by the black dual racing stripes, and has an ebony interior. Some of the highlights mentioned in the ad include the Recaro front seats, cloth and suede upholstery, MagneRide dampers, a Torsen limited-slip differential, Brembo brakes, 19-inch wheels, a black-finished roof, and the Electronics Package.
Due to some of the modifications mentioned above, this Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 could have more oomph, but the numbers are unknown, as a dyno chart does not accompany the ad. The 5.2-liter Voodoo V8 engine, which is paired with a six-speed manual transmission and rear-wheel drive, was originally good for 526 hp (534 ps/392 kW) and 429 pound-feet (582 Nm) of torque. The quarter mile took 12.5 seconds, with an exit speed of 117 mph (188 kph), and the 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) acceleration was dealt with in approximately four seconds.
Photo: Cars&Bids This muscle car had its maintenance inspection completed in August 2026, at 113,143 miles (182,086 km). The tires were rotated, and the engine oil and filter were changed in February 2026, at 111,061 miles (178,735 km). The recent service history reveals many more visits to the shop for the usual maintenance job, including in April 2025, July 2024, January 2024, and December 2023, October 2023. The 100,000-mile (160,9340 km) service was performed in the latter date, at 87,653 miles (141,064 km).
Besides the muscle car, the winning bidder will also get the OEM car cover complete with the bag, the original window sticker which has been framed, the Project 6GR wheels, the factory catalytic converters and air intake, and one key. There is a loan on this Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 , and the proceeds will be used to satisfy it, as only then the title will become available.
Now, this machine has seen a lot action. It has high mileage, quite a few issues, and a Manufacturer Buyback title, not to mention several notable modifications, and these have left their toll on its value. Nevertheless, it did go for less money than a mid-spec Toyota Corolla with only the delivery miles under its belt, and for what it’s worth, it is definitely a lot of car for the money. But knowing what you now know about it, would you have paid $27,753 in order make it yours?
Drop a line below and speak your mind about it, and once you’re done, feel free to check out this Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 in more detail here .
